Inglewood, California
  June 20, 2023

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
June 20, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:00 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************************************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales left the
dais at the hour of 2:02 p.m.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
 June 20, 2023

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Gray arrived to
  the dais at the hour of 2:03 p.m.

  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales
  returned to the dais at the hour of 2:03 p.m.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June 16, 2023,
  in the amount of $3,424,433.42, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members Gray,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman / Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD AND CONTINUED – ORDINANCE NO. 23- 12 NOT
  INTRODUCED. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public
  hearing to consider introduction of an ordinance amending or repealing various Municipal
  Code sections regulating peddling, soliciting, and sidewalk vending and adding a new
  Article 13 “Sidewalk Vendor Program” to Chapter 8 of the Municipal Code to comply with
  changes in State Law, notice had been given in the time, form, and manner as required by
  law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented a Staff Report dated June 2023.

  Jerry Tucker, Code Enforcement Manager, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there was any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke regarding food vendors being one issue but didn’t want
  the City to look like Manchester and Western or Manchester and Vermont. She stated
  that clothes were hanging on the walls at these locations, and trash was everywhere. The
  speaker added that the cleanup would cost the City more money and that there was a
  shortage of law enforcement. She also stated that she understands that people need to
  make money, but her concern was keeping the City safe and clean. She addressed the
  need to keep alleys and neighborhoods clean.

  Additionally, she reiterated her understanding of people needing to make money but
  didn’t want things for sale all over the City. She also addressed small businesses paying
  high business taxes and closing because people vend in front of their stores and coming from
  outside the community to make money. Finally, she discussed the State Law  superseding
  Inglewood’s Charter. However, she felt they should stand together as a  community to keep
  the City safe and clean.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:18 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts to adopt the 1,000 foot radius to allow for peddling,
  soliciting, and sidewalk vending, following discussion, the motion was rescinded.

  2
 June 20, 2023

  Following further discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve to continue the public hearing
  to a future date. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – RESOLUTION 23-112 ADOPTED – APPROVAL OF
  THE GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT 2022-002 (SAFETY ELEMENT). The City
  Clerk announced that the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider adoption
  of a resolution approving General Plan Amendment 2022-002 (Safety Element), notice
  had given in the time, form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no
  communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented a Staff Report dated June 20, 2023.

  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager, presented a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there was any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Faulk that the City Council does hereby: 1) Affirm Categorical
  Exemption (EA-CE-2022-117); and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-112 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, APPROVING GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT 2022-002  FOR
  THE ADOPTION OF THE SAFETY ELEMENT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

125  CLAIM DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Amended Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Jacqueline Sharpe for alleged personal injury; road condition on November 12, 2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby reject amended claim listed as A-1. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

156  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – SANTA MONICA SYSTEMS, INC. Staff report dated
  June 20, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  authorize payment of past due invoices submitted by Santa Monica Systems, Inc. for
  imaging services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $31,184.62.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 June 20, 2023

183  MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT NOS. 23-252, 23-253, AND 23-254 APPROVED
  – CITY OF LOS ANGELES, LOS ANGELES COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL
  DISTRICT (LACFCD. Staff report dated June 20, 2023, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members approve Memorandums of Agreement regarding
  cost-sharing for implementing the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program (CIMP) &
  Watershed Management Program (WMP) for the Ballona Creek Watershed and Dominguez
  Channel Watershed, and Ballona Creek Bacteria TMDL Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Memorandum of Agreement No. 23-252 between
  the City of Los Angeles, the Los Angeles County Flood Control District (LACFCD), the
  County of Los Angeles (County), and the cities Beverly Hills, Culver City, Inglewood,
  Santa Monica, and West Hollywood regarding the administration and cost-sharing for
  implementing the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring Program (CIMP) and Watershed
  Management Program (WMP) for the Ballona Creek Watershed with a total cost to the City
  of Inglewood in the amount of $91,226; 2) Approve Memorandum of Agreement No. 23-
  253 between the City of Los Angeles, the cities of Carson, El Segundo, Hawthorne,
  Inglewood, Lawndale, Lomita, the Los Angeles County Flood Control District (LACFCD),
  the County of Los Angeles (County), and the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
  regarding the administration and cost-sharing for implementing the CIMP and WMP for
  the Dominguez Channel Watershed with a total cost to the City of Inglewood in the amount
  of $190,996; and 3) Approve Memorandum of Agreement No. 23-254 between the City of
  Los Angeles, the County of Los Angeles (County), the Los Angeles County Flood Control
  District (LACFCD), and the cities of Beverly Hills, Culver City, Inglewood, and West
  Hollywood regarding the cost-sharing and implementation of the Ballona Creek Bacteria
  TMDL Project with a total cost to the City of Inglewood in the amount of $497,214.72.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  BID NO. CB-22-13 REJECTED – VINCENT PARK DECOMPOSED GRANITE
  PROJECT. Staff report dated June 20, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members reject all bid proposals for the Vincent Park Decomposed Granite
  Project (CB-22-13).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject all bid proposals; and 2) Authorize staff to re-bid
  the project.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  MAYOR AUTHORIZED TO AMEND FUNDING AGREEMENT NO. 23-210 –
  INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY (JPA).
  Staff report dated June 20, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize the Mayor to amend the funding agreement, approved as to form by the
  City Attorney, with the Inglewood Transit Connector Joint Powers Authority (JPA) to
  contribute an additional $1.5 million annually, for a total of $9.1 million annually (FY23
  dollars), as adjusted for inflation, during the operations period to support the ongoing cost
  of operating and maintaining the Inglewood Transit Connector (Project), and $3.75 million
  annually in each of the two years prior, as adjusted for inflation, to planned construction
  completion (estimated to occur in 2028) to establish a project reserve for unexpected
  operating period obligations.

  Lisa Trifiletti, Inglewood Transit Connector Project Program Manager, presented a brief
  oral report on the project's 30% operations and maintenance sources of funds as
  committed to complying with Federal Transit Administration requirements and goals.

  4
 June 20, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that

  210. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
